diagram_candidates.claim: Integer points are affine walls; A_n=(n,n+1); r_{alpha,k}(x)=2k-x; s_0(x)=-x, s_1(x)=2-x, s_1s_0(x)=x+2; the alcove action is simply transitive, and Q=Z while Q^vee=2Z under the stated convention (with the alternate convention translating by Q).
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: Several explicit coordinate maps and two lattice conventions govern a geometric action on a line. A compact picture can show the indexed alcoves and verify which reflection fixes/crosses each integer wall while making the translation subgroup scale visible.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw the real line with integer walls, label each open interval A_n, and mark A_0=(0,1). Show s_0:x↦−x across 0 and s_1:x↦2−x across 1; their product s_1s_0:x↦x+2 shifts A_n to A_{n+2}. Label translation subgroup 2Z for the stated root/coroot convention, and place the alternate convention Q=Z in a clearly separated note.
diagram_candidates.assessment: uncertain recommendation; the formulas are locally verified in the item, but a diagram should preserve the distinction between the two wall conventions rather than imply both translation lattices apply simultaneously.

diagram_candidates.claim: For m(s,t)=4, the Davis top cell has eight edges; when d_s=d_t it is a regular octagon whose barycentric subdivision is a disk, with proper cells an eight-edge boundary circle. The quotient chamber K is a square made of two triangles on their common diagonal; unequal d_s,d_t give alternating edge lengths 2d_s,2d_t.
diagram_candidates.kind: labeled polygon, subdivision, and quotient incidence diagram
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item compares the octagonal top cell, its boundary Coxeter complex, a 16-triangle subdivision, and a square quotient. These are concrete cell maps and incidence data where a diagram would reduce ambiguity.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw an octagon with alternating s/t edges and eight labeled vertices, mark the boundary cycle separately, and show the barycentric subdivision into 16 triangles as eight translates of two chamber triangles. In a paired panel draw the quotient square K split by the shared diagonal into the chains ∅<{s}<S and ∅<{t}<S. Distinguish the regular case d_s=d_t from the alternating edge-length case.
diagram_candidates.assessment: uncertain recommendation; cell counts and face maps are explicitly verified in the item, but the quotient identifications and orientation of the boundary cycle should be checked against its coset convention before drawing.

diagram_candidates.claim: In H={x∈R^4:Σx_i=0}, M(alpha) is given by x_2=−x_1, x_4=−x_3 and M(beta) by x_2=−x_3, x_4=−x_1; their intersection is R(e_1−e_2+e_3−e_4), a root-free line. Yet the absolute-order meet is 1 and M(1)=0.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: This is a geometric counterexample to identifying an intersection of moved spaces with the moved space of a meet; a schematic can make the strict containment visible.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show two planes M(alpha), M(beta) in the three-dimensional sum-zero space H intersecting in the line spanned by (1,−1,1,−1), label that this line contains no A_3 root direction, and separately show the absolute-order meet alpha∧beta=1 with M(1)=0. Mark the picture schematic rather than metric, since the defining equations live in H⊂R^4.
diagram_candidates.assessment: uncertain recommendation; the line/plane incidence is directly given by equations, while a low-dimensional projection can suggest false root incidences and needs careful labels.
